summary: How intercommunal life in late Ottoman Palestine broke down between the 1880s and 1940 as Zionist immigration, Zionist militias such as the Haganah and Irgun, Arab nationalism and British Mandate policy fed riots, assassinations and bombings.

evidence.note: host frames the story as running from the 1880s to a major bombing around 1940
1881-82 pogroms after Alexander II's killing and the May Laws drive Jewish emigration
Kishinev pogrom of 1903 and Herzl's Uganda scheme
Bar Giora and Hashomer, first Jewish armed defence groups; main span starts here
1891 petition against Zionist immigration and land sales; Husseini land dealings
Jabotinsky and Trumpeldor raise a Jewish unit from deportees held in Egypt
Ottoman wartime deportations of foreign-born Jews from Jaffa
long segment on de Haan's life in the Netherlands before emigrating
1924 assassination of de Haan by a Haganah member, called the first Zionist political murder
1929 Western Wall riots and Hebron massacre, then the Irgun split
1936-1939 Arab revolt: general strike, British suppression and death toll
1940 Haganah bombing of the Patria at Haifa ends the story

notes: No single bastard: the host says he chose a survey over a Begin or Jabotinsky episode. Zionism as primary subject is the closest fit; Mandatory Palestine (place) would also work. Origin left empty because the movement has no single country. Betar's fascist ties get only a couple of minutes, so fascism-far-right was left out. Robert places the 1881 Kirovohrad pogrom in Azerbaijan; it is in modern Ukraine. Brief modern Gaza remarks do not set reaches_present.
